how_to_use: Scored ORIGINAL premises for the What-If channel. Rubric and procedure: docs/story/IDEA_ENGINE.md. Score keys sum to score.total (weights: number_hook 10, visual_demo 15, everyday_use 10, perk_breadth 5, cost_depth 15, dilemma 15, sequel 10, feasibility 10, novelty 10). novelty_check is written by: python -I tools/ideas/novelty.py batch data/story/ideas_backlog.json --write. novelty_note records manual semantic adjustments (the tool is lexical). Numbers listed are real-world anchors; re-verify before scripting. status: candidate | chosen | scripted | released.

ideas.title: What If You Could See 10 Minutes Into the Past?
alt_titles: What If You Could Rewatch Real Life?
What If You Saw Everything That Happened 10 Minutes Ago?
ideas.premise: Wherever you look, see-through 'echoes' replay the last 10 minutes over the present: bright when fresh, faint when old, gone at exactly 10:00. You can't hear or touch them.
ideas.cold_open: Phone missing; you squint and watch a ghost of yourself put it in the fridge six minutes ago.
numbers: brain shows the world ~0.1 s late
moonlight 1.3 s old, sunlight ~8 min 20 s old
20/20 cup game = 1 in 3.5 billion by luck
brain 2% of body mass, ~20% of energy
only ~30-40% of speech is visible on lips
costs: crowds stack into a blizzard of ghosts
brain fuel: constant hunger and headaches
ideas.real_problem: The evidence deletes itself at 10:00 and it is silent: a witness nobody can believe.
ideas.dilemma: Little sister lost at a fair, 6 minutes until her echo fades: run back to tell Mom (lose the trail) or follow alone (lose the truth).
ideas.climax: Get ahead of the echo instead of chasing it; her echo fades early; the puppy's newer, brighter echo finishes the trail. Phone falls 30 m.
ideas.theme_rule: Don't chase the echo. Get to where it's going.
ideas.sequel_hook: An echo of a stranger with a yellow umbrella turns and looks at where you stand now.
ideas.part2_title: What If You Could See 10 Years Into the Past?
ideas.thumbnail: Smirking hero, one eye glowing cyan, faded ghost of himself behind; text 'ALREADY HAPPENED.'; badge '10 MIN'.
ideas.engine_needs: none (ghost actors exist); nice-to-have ghost opacity-over-time helper
ideas.novelty_note: No lexical or semantic match found. Worked example in STORY_BLUEPRINT.md section 11.

ideas.title: What If You Could Swap Places With Anyone?
alt_titles: What If You Could Swap Places With Anyone You See?
ideas.premise: Look at any person and you instantly trade places with them. You each keep your own momentum, and you need 10 seconds to recharge between swaps.
ideas.cold_open: Late for class, you swap with your friend already seated in the classroom; he appears on your porch in socks.
numbers: on flat ground you can see ~4.7 km to the horizon; from a 100 m roof ~36 km
a person falling for 2 s moves ~20 m/s (70 km/h)
10-second recharge (story rule)
perks: swap onto the stage to see the concert
costs: every swap dumps someone into your spot
momentum stays with the body (swap from a moving bus = you hit the seat at 50 km/h)
ideas.real_problem: You can never remove danger, only move it onto someone.
ideas.dilemma: A kid trapped on a burning balcony: swapping puts you in the fire with a 10-second recharge before you can swap out. Who takes your place next?
ideas.climax: Move the harm to someone built for it: swap the kid out, hold your breath 10 s, then swap with a firefighter in full gear on the ladder.
ideas.theme_rule: Never swap into a place you can't get out of.
ideas.sequel_hook: Someone swaps with you, and you wake up in a place you've never seen.
ideas.part2_title: What If You Could Swap Places With Anyone on Earth?
ideas.counter_power: someone who can't be seen (no line of sight)
ideas.thumbnail: Hero half-dissolved into a friend's silhouette, smug; text 'YOUR TURN.'
ideas.novelty_note: Semantically near 'teleport' (saturated) and body swap (InfiniteIfss 50K), but swapping positions with a person is a distinct premise with its own dilemma.

ideas.title: What If You Could Learn Any Skill in 10 Seconds?
alt_titles: What If You Could Learn Anything by Watching Once?
ideas.premise: Watch someone do something for 10 seconds and your brain has their technique, but not their body. You can hold 3 borrowed skills; a 4th pushes out the oldest.
ideas.cold_open: You watch a street juggler for 10 seconds, then juggle five oranges at the checkout.
numbers: ~10,000 hours of practice for experts (Ericsson's violinist study)
10,000 h vs 10 s = 3.6 million times faster
mirror neurons found in monkeys in the 1990s
CPR: 100-120 compressions a minute, 5-6 cm deep
perks: play a song at grandma's party
costs: technique without the body: your ankles can't take the kickflip
you copy flaws too (an out-of-tune guitarist)
ideas.real_problem: Learning something new means losing something you love.
ideas.dilemma: Someone collapses; learning CPR from the lifeguard means dropping grandma's piano song, the slot you swore to keep.
ideas.climax: Drop the song, do CPR to a remembered rhythm, keep going until the ambulance.
ideas.theme_rule: Borrow skills. Earn the ones you love.
ideas.sequel_hook: A kid watches YOU for 10 seconds, and now has all three of your skills.
ideas.part2_title: What If You Could Learn Any Skill in 1 Second?
ideas.counter_power: a copier who learns from you / skill eraser
ideas.thumbnail: Hero casually juggling five things including a flaming torch, half-lidded; text 'TOO EASY.'; badge '10 SEC'.
ideas.novelty_note: Lexical RELATED only via '10 seconds'. Nearest semantic neighbours: IQ/genius titles (crowded) and 'Knew Everything in the World' (82K); the skill-slot mechanic differs.

ideas.title: What If Your Voice Was 100x Louder?
alt_titles: What If Your Whisper Was a Scream?
ideas.premise: Your voice comes out about 100 times louder (+66 dB). Normal talking lands past the pain threshold, and a whisper sounds like a lawnmower. Your hearing stays normal.
ideas.cold_open: You whisper 'pass the salt' and every glass on the table rings; the dog leaves the room.
numbers: every +10 dB sounds about twice as loud
talking ~60 dB -> ~126 dB; pain threshold ~120-130 dB
long exposure above 85 dB risks hearing damage
a singer shattered a glass at ~105 dB on TV
shouts don't trigger avalanches (myth)
~70 million deaf people use sign languages
perks: call the dog from three blocks away
stop a fight with one word
costs: you hurt the ears of everyone near you
glass shatters when you hum the wrong note
ideas.real_problem: You can't talk to the people you love without hurting them, so you stop talking.
ideas.dilemma: Night fire in an apartment block, alarms dead, firefighters 6 minutes away: one shout wakes 40 people but could damage your little brother's ears. 'Their ears... or their lives.'
ideas.climax: Learned control: run to the courtyard, cup your hands upward away from family, one word. A planted resonance hum shatters a stuck window.
ideas.theme_rule: Say less. Mean it more.
ideas.sequel_hook: Someone answers your shout from across the city, even louder.
ideas.part2_title: What If Your Voice Was 1,000x Louder?
ideas.thumbnail: Hero mid-shout, shockwave rings, windows cracking; text 'SHHH.'; badge '100x'.
ideas.novelty_note: Related: IFshiftTales 'Got Louder and Couldn't Stop' (39K). Ours is a fixed multiplier with sign-language and resonance arcs.

ideas.title: What If You Could See Everyone's Stats?
alt_titles: What If Real Life Had a HUD?
ideas.premise: Game-style bars float over everyone: energy, mood, strength, honesty. You can't see your own.
ideas.cold_open: Choosing gym teams, you read STRENGTH 91 over the quiet kid nobody picks. You pick him. You win.
numbers: resting heart rate 60-100 bpm
polygraphs aren't reliable enough for most courts
feeling thirsty means you're already ~1-2% low on water
perks: ask the teacher for an extension when MOOD is high
costs: you see what people hide (Mom's HAPPINESS behind a smile)
ideas.real_problem: You see a friend's HEALTH bar dropping, and nobody else can.
ideas.dilemma: Tell him how you know and expose yourself, or watch him collapse at the game.
ideas.climax: Get him to the nurse with the truth; the bar stops falling.
ideas.theme_rule: People aren't numbers. Numbers are where you start.
ideas.sequel_hook: A stranger walks past with every stat reading '???'.

ideas.title: What If You Could Make Anything 10x Bigger?
alt_titles: What If Everything You Touched Grew 10x?
ideas.premise: Touch an object and it grows 10x in every direction until you touch it again. It also gets 1,000x heavier but only 100x stronger.
ideas.cold_open: Last cookie; one tap and it's the size of a bike wheel, crashing off the plate.
numbers: square-cube law (Galileo, 1638): 10x size = 100x strength, 1,000x weight
a 200 g phone becomes 200 kg
a 10x ant would suffocate: insects breathe through tiny tubes
costs: big things break under their own weight
ideas.real_problem: You must touch it to shrink it back, and a giant thing rolling away can't be touched.
ideas.dilemma: People trapped on a flooding underpass: enlarge the small inflatable boat, but at 10x it's too heavy to carry to the water. Grow it where it is, or not at all.
ideas.climax: Carry the small thing to the right place first, then grow it (theme rule); the rope you enlarged earlier is 100x stronger.
ideas.theme_rule: Bigger isn't stronger. Put it in place, then grow it.
ideas.sequel_hook: Something enormous is growing on the edge of town, and you didn't touch it.
ideas.part2_title: What If You Could Make Anything 100x Bigger?
ideas.thumbnail: Hero holding a normal phone next to a 10x phone crushing a car; text 'HEAVY.'; badge '10x'.
ideas.novelty_note: Tool: CLOSE to 'Woke Up 10x Bigger' (Hypothetically2026, 1K views) and RELATED to '10x Bigger or 10x Smaller' (9.8K). Manual 6: growing OBJECTS with square-cube costs is a different premise, but the title reads similar, so differentiate in the thumbnail (a giant object, not a giant hero).

ideas.title: What If You Could Jump 100x Higher?
alt_titles: What If You Could Jump Over Buildings?
ideas.premise: Your legs push 100x harder: a normal 0.5 m jump becomes 50 m, about 16 floors. Your bones and skin stay normal, so going up is free and coming down isn't.
ideas.cold_open: Cat stuck in a tree: one hop, grab it, and then the long, worrying fall begins.
numbers: 50 m jump: ~3.2 s up, ~6.4 s in the air
landing at ~31 m/s (113 km/h)
a flea jumps about 100x its body length
ski jumpers survive because the landing slope matches their fall
perks: fastest route to school over the rooftops
ideas.real_problem: There's always a way up. There isn't always a way down.
ideas.dilemma: A kid trapped on a 12th-floor balcony: you can reach him, but you can't land carrying him.
ideas.climax: Aim the fall at the curved stadium roof and slide down it like a ski jumper.
ideas.theme_rule: Never jump higher than your way down.
ideas.sequel_hook: Mid-jump, you see someone standing on the clouds, waiting.
ideas.part2_title: What If You Could Jump 1,000x Higher?
ideas.thumbnail: Hero mid-air above suburb rooftops, smug, looking down; text 'NOW WHAT.'; badge '100x'.

ideas.title: What If You Could Copy Anything You Touch?
alt_titles: What If Everything You Touched Had a Twin?
ideas.premise: Touch an object and a perfect copy pops out beside it. The copy's mass comes out of your body.
ideas.cold_open: Last slice of pizza, two hands reach; you tap it, there are two, and your jeans feel looser.
numbers: 1 kg of body fat ~ 7,700 kcal
copied banknotes share serial numbers (how fakes are caught)
carriers block phones with duplicate IMEI numbers
a small fire extinguisher weighs about 5 kg
perks: a copy of the house key for everyone
costs: every copy costs you its weight
copied money and phones are illegal or blocked
ideas.real_problem: You can only give away so much of yourself.
ideas.dilemma: A wildfire reaches your street: 8 houses, one extinguisher. Each copy costs 5 kg of you, and you can afford 3.
ideas.climax: Copy the small thing that does the big job: the 200 g hydrant wrench and hose couplings, not the extinguishers.
ideas.theme_rule: Copy the small thing that does the big job.
ideas.sequel_hook: You find a perfect copy of your house key that you never made.

ideas.title: What If Your Eyes Were 10x Faster?
alt_titles: What If You Saw Everything in Slow Motion?
ideas.premise: Your eyes and visual brain take in 10x more frames per second, so the world looks 10x slower, but your body moves at normal speed.
ideas.cold_open: A glass slides off the table; you watch it fall forever, still can't move fast enough, and slide your foot under it.
numbers: humans see flicker up to ~60 Hz; flies ~250 Hz
movies are 24 frames a second: at 10x, a slideshow
LED and fluorescent lights flicker at 100-120 Hz
a 10 m fall takes 1.4 s, which feels like 14 s
ideas.real_problem: You see disaster coming in slow motion, and you're no faster than anyone else.
ideas.dilemma: Scaffolding tips over a kid: 1.4 real seconds. Run (too slow) or think: find the one small move that changes everything.
ideas.climax: Kick the wheel lock on the rolling cart so it slides under the falling frame.
ideas.theme_rule: When you can't be faster, be earlier.
ideas.sequel_hook: One person moves so fast that even you see them as a blur.
ideas.part2_title: What If Your Eyes Were 100x Faster?
ideas.thumbnail: A ball frozen inches from the hero's calm, bored face; text 'BORING.'; badge '10x'.
ideas.novelty_note: Tool novelty 3 (false lexical match to '10x Faster'). Manual 5: an adjacent move on Reaction Time 10x (4.5M) and Reflexes 100x (351K). Proven demand, but differentiate hard with the strobe and slideshow costs.

ideas.title: What If You Could Stretch 10x Longer?
alt_titles: What If Your Body Was Made of Rubber?
ideas.premise: Your body stretches like rubber up to 10x its length, but your volume stays the same: the longer you get, the thinner and weaker you are.
ideas.cold_open: Remote across the room; your arm unspools along the floor while the dog chases your hand.
numbers: 10x longer = 1/10 the thickness = ~1/10 the strength
surface area x3.2, so you lose heat ~3x faster
an octopus can squeeze through any hole bigger than its beak
perks: clean the gutters from the lawn
hug the whole family at once
ideas.real_problem: The longer you get, the weaker you are, exactly when you need to be strong.
ideas.dilemma: Kids stranded across a 15 m gap in a collapsed footbridge: become the bridge at your weakest, or leave them.
ideas.climax: Be the rope, not the bridge: anchor both ends at partial stretch and carry one kid at a time.
ideas.theme_rule: Only stretch as far as you need.
ideas.sequel_hook: Someone pulls you from the other end.
ideas.part2_title: What If You Could Stretch 100x Longer?
ideas.thumbnail: Hero lounging on the couch, arm snaking through the house to the fridge; text 'LAZY.'; badge '10x'.

ideas.title: What If You Could Slow Down Anything You Look At?
alt_titles: What If Your Eyes Could Slow Time?
ideas.move: flip_direction (stop all time -> slow only the centre of your gaze)
ideas.premise: Whatever is in the sharp centre of your vision moves 10x slower; everything else stays at full speed. Blinking resets it.
ideas.cold_open: Toast pops; you stare, it floats; you pluck it from the air while Dad's coffee splashes at normal speed.
numbers: the sharp centre of vision is ~2 degrees, about your thumbnail at arm's length
you blink 15-20 times a minute
the fovea is ~1% of the retina but uses about half the visual cortex
perks: stare down the slowest school clock hand (you're late now)
costs: only one thing at a time
what you don't look at is full speed
ideas.real_problem: You can only protect what you're looking at, and danger is always somewhere else.
ideas.dilemma: A toddler heading for the pool and a falling flowerpot, two directions: which do you look at?
ideas.climax: Move until both are in one gaze (line them up using the patio window's reflection) and hold without blinking.
ideas.theme_rule: Change where you stand, not just where you look.
ideas.sequel_hook: A figure you can't look at directly: your eyes slide off it.
ideas.part2_title: What If You Could Stop Anything You Look At?
ideas.counter_power: someone who can't be looked at
ideas.thumbnail: Hero staring calmly at a baseball hanging inches from his face, frozen streaks; text 'LOOK.'; badge '10x'.
ideas.novelty_note: NOVEL lexically; semantic cousin of stop/freeze time (saturated). The gaze-only rule makes the dilemma new.

ideas.title: What If You Were Magnetic?
alt_titles: What If You Were as Magnetic as an MRI?
ideas.premise: Flex and your body puts out an MRI-strength field (~3 tesla). You can't aim it: it pulls all steel around you, and at half the distance it pulls eight times harder.
ideas.cold_open: Late, keys lost; hold out a hand and the keys, four spoons and every fridge magnet fly to you.
numbers: Earth's field ~50 millionths of a tesla; fridge magnet ~0.005 T; MRI 1.5-3 T
half the distance = 8x the pull
MRI scanners have yanked oxygen tanks across rooms
pacemakers: keep magnets ~15 cm away
aluminium cans ignore magnets
costs: wipes bank cards and key cards
ideas.real_problem: You can't aim it, and some people carry steel inside their bodies (pacemakers).
ideas.dilemma: A driverless van rolling toward a market; full power would stop it but could throw a neighbour's pacemaker out of rhythm. 'The van... or the man.'
ideas.climax: Run closer to the van and away from him, then pulse (don't pull) three times.
ideas.theme_rule: Pulse, don't pull.
ideas.sequel_hook: Every magnet on the fridge drops at once: someone repels metal.
ideas.part2_title: What If You Were 1,000x More Magnetic?

blood rushes to your head upside down

ideas.title: What If You Could Mute Anything?
alt_titles: What If You Could Turn Off Any Sound?
ideas.premise: Point at anything and its sound disappears, cancelled like noise-cancelling headphones, until you unmute it.
ideas.cold_open: Your brother's 7 a.m. drum practice; you point; silence; he keeps drumming, confused.
numbers: noise-cancelling works by playing the sound's mirror image
smoke alarms must reach ~85 dB at 3 m
sound travels 343 m/s
costs: muted things can't warn you (car horns)
you can't unmute what you can't see
ideas.real_problem: Warnings exist for a reason, and the alarm you muted as a prank is still muted.
ideas.dilemma: Fire at a packed concert: the alarm is drowned out. Mute the band in front of 3,000 fans and get exposed, or let the alarm go unheard. 'The music... or the message.'
ideas.climax: Mute the concert, unmute the alarm you silenced weeks ago, and guide the crowd in silence.
ideas.theme_rule: Silence is a tool, not a hiding place.
ideas.sequel_hook: A voice gets through your mute anyway.

ideas.title: What If You Could Control Temperature?
alt_titles: What If You Could Move Heat With Your Hands?
ideas.premise: You can pull heat out of things or push it in, but you don't create it: cooling a drink heats your hands.
ideas.cold_open: Cocoa too hot; you hold it and it's perfect in a second, and steam rises off your fingers.
